what: Dafny proofs about the code that guards money: formal/dafny/*.dfy. Written up in docs/evidence/formal-proofs.md.
verifier: Dafny program verifier finished with 172 verified, 0 errors

theorems.Terms.TermsBytesInjective: equal canonical bytes (the input of SHA-256) imply equal terms, as maps, recursively
theorems.Terms.FieldChangeChangesBytes: changing, adding or dropping any one field of a terms object changes its canonical bytes
theorems.Terms.SameCanonicalFormIffSameMembers: the canonical form depends on the object as a map only (member order is irrelevant)
theorems.Jcs.SerInjective: JCS serialisation of JSON without numbers is injective (a decoder is its left inverse: Jcs.ParseSer)
theorems.Utf8.EncodeInjective: UTF-8 is injective on well-formed UTF-16 (Utf8.DecodeEncode); Terms.SerWellFormed: JCS output is well-formed
theorems.Money.ToCentsOfFromCents: cents -> string -> cents is the identity on 0..2^53-1
theorems.Money.FromCentsOfToCents: string -> cents -> string is the identity on every string toCents accepts
theorems.Money.AcceptedIffRendering: toCents accepts exactly the strings fromCents writes, and refuses everything else
theorems.Money.ToCentsIsExact: the cents are exactly 100 times the written decimal number (no rounding)
theorems.Limit.PaidAloneIffWithinLimit: code pays alone exactly when the limit is set, the currency is the limit's and amount_cents <= limit_cents
theorems.Limit.PaidAloneIffWrittenAmountAtMostLim: the cent comparison is the exact comparison of the written decimal amounts
theorems.Limit.CapPassesIffAtMostCap: capRefusal lets a payment pass the cap exactly when there is no cap or cents <= cap
